flags.title: The nightly export fits the Free plan's limits
flags.dod: A staging fire of the nightly export with a large synthetic seed stays inside the Free plan's per-invocation CPU and D1 query limits (read from current Cloudflare docs), measured with Workers Logs; if it does not fit, the export moves into a Workflow or pages; a put of an existing exports/ key on staging is refused (never-overwrite) (§data.export)
flags.notes: Claims review Unknown 1 and 4: server/scheduled.ts runs the export inside the 15-minute cron (20 SELECTs, SHA-256 per table, JSON.stringify of all, R2 head and put); Free limits are tight and real data plus group 4's new tables grow it. server/nightly-export.ts relies on onlyIf etagDoesNotMatch '*', which the R2 docs do not spell out. Needs observability on in wrangler.jsonc. With B-822 and B-999.

flags.notes: Claims review Unknown 3: S-07 tested hand-written validation only; the real Zod CPU check owed since D-455 and D-458 was never run. B-1005 (SDK Zod helper) makes it matter more, so run it after B-1005.

flags.title: A job's deadline covers a step's worst-case retries
flags.dod: defineJob refuses a running deadline shorter than one step's worst case (STEP_RETRY attempts times the step timeout plus the backoff delays), computed from jobs/runtime/workflow.ts, not a fixed 5 minutes; a test covers it; the default and per-job deadlines are checked against it
flags.notes: Claims review Wrong 2: jobs/runtime/define.ts:81 only checks over 5 minutes, but one step can take about 21 minutes (4 attempts of up to 5 minutes plus 5, 10 and 20 s backoff, jobs/runtime/workflow.ts:17-19; Workflows applies the timeout per attempt). The 15/30 and default 30/60 values are builder picks, not platform limits. Slice write: jobs/runtime.
